content:
One of my favorite iPhone cases has returned with a fresh new look. I’ve used several generations of BitmoLab’s GAMEBABY case, and fell in love with it the moment I tried it—it feels like an accessory specifically designed to awaken my sense of nostalgia. The biggest selling point of this case is that it’s not a separate accessory you have to carry around and remember to charge; instead, it’s a cleverly designed regular iPhone case that can also serve as a controller with physical buttons for playing your favorite Game Boy ROMs (and other games). It perfectly embodies the spirit of “work smart, not hard.” It requires no batteries, no Bluetooth, and the setup is very straightforward. If you’re into any form of retro game emulation, you definitely need to check out this product.

Be sure to watch our hands-on video to see the case in action!

The design of this case is very simple, yet extremely ingenious. It uses a two-piece design, where the bottom half is the controller. During everyday non-gaming use, it feels no different from a regular case. You get:

  • Physical side buttons for the lock button, volume buttons, and action buttons
  • Cutouts for the USB-C port, speakers, buttons, and camera control
  • A protective bumper around the screen and camera module
  • Hardshell plastic protection

But the magic lies in the bottom half. That’s where the game controls are located—the buttons are well-made, feel solid, and are very satisfying to press. But how exactly does it work?

How It Works

Again, the brilliance of this design is that there are no electronic components inside, so no pairing is required. The way it works is that each physical game button has a small capacitive contact that mimics the action of your finger touching the screen. This way, the iPhone thinks you’re pressing the on-screen controls, while you feel like you’re pressing real buttons. The technology is the same as the soft capacitive tips on those cheap styluses.

There’s a simple setup step to ensure the physical buttons align with the on-screen control positions. BitmoLabs provides all the necessary instructions via a QR code on the packaging. However, it works through the Delta Emulator app on the App Store. This app is completely free to use, with no in-app purchases. After downloading the app, GAMEBABY offers a downloadable custom skin that places the emulator’s virtual buttons directly beneath the physical buttons. This skin is also free (you can download it even if you don’t have the case).

Once you’ve installed the skin in the Delta Emulator app, you’re ready to play. All you need to do is detach the bottom half of the case, flip it over, and reattach it to your iPhone—this positions the control buttons over the iPhone’s screen, giving you the feel of real physical buttons when playing retro games. When you’re done gaming, slide out the controller section, flip it back, and reattach it, and it becomes a regular case again.

My Experience Using It

As I mentioned at the beginning, I have zero resistance to anything retro gaming-related—it always triggers my urge to replay those classic Pokémon games from years past. This case not only makes gaming more convenient, but also provides a near-frictionless experience. No need to remember to bring anything, no charging, no pairing. For me, remembering to carry an extra accessory is always the biggest hassle with tech accessories, so this case completely eliminates that barrier.

Using it, I can also feel that BitmoLabs has significantly improved the build quality of this case. The buttons have excellent tactile feedback—they bounce right back the moment you lift your finger, and there’s been no button failure during gaming. I mainly use it to play all the classic Pokémon titles, which are relatively casual games that don’t require lightning-fast reaction times. Even for games that demand quick reflexes, this case handles them well.

There’s one trade-off to be aware of: there’s no MagSafe functionality. Because the case is split into two parts and the bottom half already has stuff going on, there’s essentially no way to incorporate MagSafe. If you absolutely need MagSafe in a case, then this one might not be for you. That said, if you have MagSafe accessories (I personally have a ton), it’s easy enough to just take the case off to use them. The case also doesn’t have a camera control cover—not a big deal, but worth considering.

Price and Availability

GAMEBABY is available on the BitmoLab website and Amazon, starting at $24.99. There are three versions: GameBaby Color, GameBaby Retro, and the newest GameBaby Transparent (the one I’m showing). GameBaby Transparent is currently only available for the iPhone 17 Pro Max, and it’s a limited release of just 500 units, available exclusively on the BitmoLab website. The other versions are compatible with iPhone 15 Pro and above, and can be purchased on both Amazon and the official website. Again, with no electronics, batteries, or Bluetooth, they’ve been able to keep the price down to $25—which is an absolute steal for such a well-designed case!

Conclusion

If you’re like me and love revisiting retro games on your iPhone, then this case is absolutely the one for you. It’s affordable, lightweight, easy to set up, and genuinely enhances the experience of playing emulated retro games on iPhone. Combining physical buttons with the iPhone’s excellent haptic engine really does make it feel like you’re playing on a retro game console. With the wave of retro Pokémon game mods currently trending on social media, there’s no better time to relax with this case and revisit these classic games.

What do you think about this case? Would you consider getting one? Have you tried using it? Drop a comment below and let’s discuss!
